correctness.rationale: PASS: Stop-loss functions C_mu(t)=E(X-t)_+ characterize one-dimensional convex order at equal mean and depend continuously on weakly convergent probability measures on [0,1], so the union of both oriented orders is closed. For a distinct comparable pair, mixing one member with the mean-m endpoint Bernoulli and compressing the other toward m retains an interior strict inequality yet reverses a high-strike inequality. For an equal pair, the explicit upper two-point law ((2(1-m)/(2-m)) at m/2; m/(2-m) at 1) and lower two-point law ((1-m)/(1+m) at 0; 2m/(1+m) at (1+m)/2), both mixed with a compressed common law, have opposed endpoint put/call inequalities. These perturbations approach their originals in weak topology and keep mean exactly m. Smooth convolution after compression and an arbitrarily small smooth positive exponential-tilt mixture preserve exact mean and strict incomparability. At m=0,1 the theorem is correctly excluded. Independently checked endpoint law means and m=1/2 rational stop-loss gaps ±1/240. The all-law density is analytic, not deduced from finite checks.

The theorem handles every interior mean, diagonal and strict pairs, as well as positive smooth representatives, and exposes a sharp topological distinction from totally ordered fixed-support three-point fibers. This is a complete motivated structural result, not a renamed textbook criterion.
